result:
A race condition is a bug where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of two or more things running at once, such as two processes that both read, then modify, the same file and end up overwriting or interleaving each other's work.

For a shared log, always append with `>>` (never `>` or read-then-rewrite), and take a lock around anything that is more than a single short line:

```sh
(
  flock 9
  printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$msg" >&9
) 9>>"$LOG"
```

`>>` opens the file in append mode, so the kernel moves each write to the current end of the file and writers can't clobber each other. `flock` then makes each writer wait its turn, so multi-line or large entries can't interleave, and the lock is released automatically when the subshell exits.

This relies on every writer using the same `flock` pattern, and on a local filesystem; on NFS neither append mode nor `flock` is dependable, so there you would send entries to a single logger process (for example `logger`/syslog) instead.
